slides.title: Peter Steinberger joins OpenAI Peter Steinberger joins OpenAI
slides.text: Peter Steinberger joins OpenAI Peter Steinberger joins OpenAI Peter Steinberger, creator of OpenClaw (an open-source AI agent), is joining OpenAI to help make AI agents accessible to everyone Despite OpenClaw's viral success and potential to become a major company, Steinberger prioritizes building over business operations After meeting with major AI labs in San Francisco, he chose OpenAI as the best partner to advance his vision while keeping OpenClaw open-source OpenClaw will transition to an independent foundation with OpenAI's sponsorship, maintaining its community-driven approach Steinberger aims to create agents simple enough for non-technical users while accessing cutting-edge models and research at OpenAI https://steipete.me/posts/2026/openclaw How OpenClaw Works: OpenClaw operates locally on the user's computer, granting it access to files and hardware. This allows it to solve real-world problems autonomously, such as converting audio formats or managing smart home devices without pre-programmed instructions Up to 80% of current apps may be substituted by apps managing data through natural conversation OpenClaw stores "memories" as local Markdown files owned by the user Peter favors simple Unix CLI tools over complex protocols like MCP, simple formats (a "personality-driven" soul.md ) https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw - 214K stars OpenClaw News Support for Sonnet 4.6, GPT 5.3 Codex, up to 1M token window you can configure to use different models for different tasks Anthropic ban of using pro or max subscriptions with OpenClaw https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2HiHDIFStzg - use OpenAI Agents can spawn sub-agents; better interfaces for Slack, Telegram, and Discord - real-time message streaming and interactive UI components like buttons and modals Apple watch support, iOS share extension Crash recovery via a write-ahead queue, support for Hugging Face open-source models, and over 80 security and bug fixes https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m_l9pUKLiXo - how Peter works (2 Macs, tools, AI techniques)

slides.title: Peter Steinberger & Mac Mini Sales Peter Steinberger
slides.text: Peter Steinberger & Mac Mini Sales Peter Steinberger has been jokingly crowned as Apple's "world's greatest Mac salesman" for inadvertently driving massive Mac Mini sales through OpenClaw . The OpenClaw phenomenon has created measurable supply shortages across Apple's Mac lineup. The impact on Mac Mini availability and market dynamics is well-documented: https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/openclaw-fueled-ordering-frenzy-creates-apple-mac-shortage-delivery-for-high-unified-memory-units-now-ranges-from-6-days-to-6-weeks The M4 Mac Mini emerged as the "hardware of choice" for the decentralized AI movement for several practical reasons: 24/7 operation; iMessage access; Inexpensive; compact 16GB base model is OK. 24GB is recommended if you are also planning to run local models The phenomenon has repositioned Mac Mini from a standard desktop into a "dedicated AI server" or personal "JARVIS" Chinese Giants Offer OpenClaw Baidu is integrating OpenClaw into its main search app, which has about 700 million monthly active users Moonshot AI launched Kimi Claw, a browser‑native/cloud‑hosted version of OpenClaw running on kimi.com - includes 40GB cloud storage and access to 5K+ community skills Alibaba and Tencent also working on similar offerings 370+ skills - MIT license https://github.com/aiskillstore/marketplace OpenClaw Tutorial - using VPS & Opus 4.6 & Codex https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vte-fDoZczE Connecting Telegram for messaging and voice transcription Organizing conversations into topic-specific Telegram group chats, and enabling coding and GitHub skills so the bot can write and commit code Open Claw's core concepts: skills (markdown-based capability files), memory systems (persistent and daily memory files), identity/user profile files, the heartbeat system for periodic automated tasks, and cron jobs for scheduled reminders or operations Treat the bot like an untrusted assistant for security and recommends spending time customizing its configuration files for the best results. slides.title: SaaS >> Local Hackable Skills Substitute Google NotebookLM
slides.text: SaaS >> Local Hackable Skills Substitute Google NotebookLM with 214 custom "skills" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4-gKmXzvEmc NotebookLM is great and useful, but limited to a fixed menu James has built 214 unique skills that are tailored to specific business needs, such as creating YouTube scripts or generating slide decks James uses these skills within Claude, Claude Co-work, and Claude Code. But they can be also used with other models (Gemini, ...) and other agent platforms (Manus, ...) James predicts that within 30 days, AI "employees" will move from just performing tasks on command to proactively asking users what work needs to be done James concludes that the education industry is splitting into two groups: .. Content Creators (losing to AI) .. Transformation Facilitators - win by using AI skills allowing them to focus on direct human interaction and results Human >> AI SaaS  >> AI Enabled SaaS >> Local Hackable Skills (OpenClaw or similar) NotebookLM is a Google AI “research assistant” It lets you create notebooks, upload sources (Docs, PDFs, web pages, YouTube transcripts, etc.), and then ask questions that are answered strictly from those materials, with citations It can auto-generate summaries, outlines, study guides, and tables comparing information across sources, plus podcast-style audio overviews (mp3 files) Unlike a general chatbot, it doesn’t roam the web; it focuses on synthesizing what you’ve loaded, which reduces hallucinations and keeps everything traceable Typical uses include studying, literature reviews, project research, and shared team notebooks for centralized, queryable knowledge. Compare: OpenClaw, GravityClaw, ZeroClaw (in Rust), Meta Manus, Abacus DeepAgent

slides.title: Claude Sonnet 4.6 Claude Sonnet 4.6 is Anthropic’s
slides.text: Claude Sonnet 4.6 Claude Sonnet 4.6 is Anthropic’s new “workhorse” model High‑throughput, cost‑efficient daily driver for knowledge workers Pricing remains the same as 4.5 ($3/$15 per 1M in/out tokens) 1 Mln token context window Becomes the default on the free plan Performance approaches or rivals Opus 4.6 on many benchmarks Coding, tool use, and “agentic” abilities Creating PowerPoints, manipulating Excel, navigating complex UIs, and handling long, multi‑step work products like documents, slides, diagrams, and spreadsheets Much stronger on Computer-Use benchmark - seeing the screen, “clicking” a mouse, and typing on a keyboard, ... Protection from prompt injection (safer for OpenClaw) Big jump on “Humanity’s Last Exam” and ARC‑AGI‑2 Big jump on VendingBench and strategy Sonnet 4.6 supports adaptive reasoning (“thinking tokens”), so it can scale the depth of its reasoning effort up or down per task Context compaction in beta to auto‑summarize older context near limit Web search and fetch tools can now auto‑write and execute code to filter and process results Code execution, memory, programmatic tool calling, and tool search are generally available, including in integrations like Claude for Excel with MCP connectors Outperforms Opus 4.6 on GDP‑Val AA (working with docs, slides, diagrams, spreadsheets) Sonnet 4.6 - Programmatic Tool Calling - the agent writes actual code to invoke tools in a sandbox environment Instead of LLM executing several tools in sequence using intermediate JSON, the agent writes and executes one script (in safe sandbox) to do all the steps - and return the final answer Less tokens (keeping intermediate JSONs out of the context window), less context window pollution, improved accuracy Claude now writes code to post-process and filter web search results before they enter context window Tool Search helps agents find specific tools within MCP servers http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8dVCSPXG6Mw Sonnet is cheaper than Opus, but uses more reasoning tokens So it may be beneficial to continue using Claude Opus

slides.text: AI Updates xAI has launched Grok 4.2 (Grok 420) , introducing a novel "Society of Mind" architecture integrated directly into its inference Unlike standard models, it utilizes a 4-agent collaboration system where specialized agents debate in parallel before delivering a final response. The team consists of: Grok (The Captain): Coordinates, synthesizes final answers Harper: Performs real-time research via the X (Twitter) Benjamin: Handles logic, coding, and math verification Lucas: Acts as a contrarian "wildcard" to prevent groupthink and encourage divergent thinking This architecture is optimized via reinforcement learning, making it more efficient than running four separate clones Early performance indicators are strong, with Grok 4.2 variants being the only profitable models in a recent live stock trading arena The model aims for "agentic performance" over static benchmarks, focusing on long-horizon, real-world utility. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d4tbdFpcuSQ

slides.title: Claude in Excel & PowerPoint Claude in Excel
slides.text: Claude in Excel & PowerPoint Claude in Excel https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BX2PxxM15Zc Tim Vipond tests Claude's Excel capabilities by challenging it to build a complete three-statement financial model from scratch. He uploads a blank CFI template containing only assumptions and historical data, with all forecast formulas deleted, then prompts Claude to complete the forecast. Using a simple prompt, Claude systematically rebuilds the entire model, creating formulas for income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement, plus supporting schedules for working capital and capital structure. The AI follows proper financial modeling methodology, building components in logical order and achieving a balanced balance sheet. When compared side-by-side with CFI's completed course model, all numbers match exactly, demonstrating Claude built fully integrated, dynamic financial statements with proper formula linkages. While formatting needed minor refinements, Claude successfully replicated complex financial modeling that typically requires extensive training, completing the task in minutes with remarkable accuracy. Claude in PowerPoint https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gxL6-rg3SoY Claude has been integrated directly into Microsoft PowerPoint as a free add-in that transforms data creation workflows. Available only to paid Claude users with Mac team or enterprise accounts, this tool converts CSV files and Excel spreadsheets into complete presentations with visuals, charts, and branded templates in under 30 seconds. Users simply upload their data, provide specific instructions about what they want, and Claude generates professional slide decks including headers, graphs, and formatting. While the AI handles 90% of the work, users can still customize colors, logos, and layouts as needed. This integration could disrupt consulting industries that rely heavily on presentation creation, allowing smaller businesses to compete with larger firms without expensive analyst teams. The tool is particularly valuable for creating client reports, training materials, investor pitches, and weekly updates, potentially saving users hundreds of hours annually that were previously spent on manual slide creation.

slides.title: Using memory can cut token costs by 80%
slides.text: Using memory can cut token costs by 80% Memory reduces token costs by up to 80% Manolo Remiddi introduces a "Noiseless" AI memory protocol for his open-source project, Resonant OS. This system reduces token costs by up to 80% by stripping "human noise" from conversations and compressing old data into a pure data format that remains searchable via hashes. Key features include "Awareness Agents" that inject relevant documents into the prompt only when needed, and a "Logician" that enforces rules through code to prevent hallucinations. For security, he advocates for a "Paranoia Mode," providing a framework for users to build an AI "Shield" that scans code for threats. Ultimately, Remiddi envisions a decentralized "Resonant Economy" where AI agents collaborate and trade services via a DAO and crypto micropayments, moving away from corporate-centralized models. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AGxcQ-j64Ms

slides.text: Build a 10-agent OpenClaw Team Build a 10-agent OpenClaw Team by Nathaniel Whittemore https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HzVYgpMxMLE https://openclaw.ai The episode covers how the host built a 10‑agent OpenClaw team, why it’s valuable, and where it falls short The author explains using a Claude project as a patient build partner so even non‑technical users can set up agents and mission control on modest hardware, like a dedicated Mac mini with remote access tools He outlines OpenClaw’s markdown‑based architecture (agent identity, tools, user profile, heartbeat tasks, cron jobs) He describes agents for coding, continuous AI research, project management, and personal task tracking, emphasizing mobile chat control and persistent background work He notes current limitations—flaky heartbeats, security concerns with early skills, and the complexity of custom dashboards—but argues anyone willing to invest time can now build practical, always‑on digital “employees.”

slides.title: AI Updates Why The INSANE AI Datacenter Build
slides.text: AI Updates Why The INSANE AI Datacenter Build Out Make Sense https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qFpps5Ur-qs The massive AI datacenter buildout may seem irrational given that current language models only need around 2,000 H100 GPUs for training, but AI video generation could justify this scale . Video tokens require dramatically more compute than text tokens, with 128,000 text tokens equaling just 3.6 seconds of 720p video. However, the real justification lies in AI world models for robotics and autonomous driving simulation, not entertainment videos. These models, like Nvidia's Cosmos, can simulate diverse environments for robot training without needing manual programming at scale. This makes the datacenter investment potentially viable for training robots across industries rather than just generating content for human consumption. Hostinger - a web hosting provider offering shared hosting, VPS, and cloud solutions starting at $1.99 per month - https://www.hostinger.com Features AMD EPYC processors, NVMe SSD storage, and user-friendly tools including hPanel control panel and Kodee AI assistant The platform provides automatic backups, 24/7 support, global data centers, and one-click installations, making it popular among WordPress users, developers, and small businesses seeking affordable, reliable hosting Hostinger's AI-oriented offerings include: Horizons (no-code AI web app builder) Kodee AI Assistant (performs 350+ tasks like website migration, content creation, DNS management, and security scanning) AI Website Builder Tools (AI Writer, Image Generator, Logo Maker, Blog Generator, SEO Assistant, Heatmap Generator) OpenClaw AI Hosting with pre-integrated OpenAI and Anthropic credits Hostinger Reach for email marketing LLM optimization capabilities WordPress AI plugin These features enable users to quickly launch and manage websites without technical complexity while maintaining strong performance and security.

slides.title: Ollama Ollama supports subagents & web search in
slides.text: Ollama Ollama supports subagents & web search in Claude Code No MCP servers or API keys required. ollama launch claude --model minimax-m2.5:cloud Subagents can run tasks in parallel, such as file search, code exploration, and research, each in their own context. Some models will naturally trigger subagents when needed (minimax-m2.5, glm-5, kimi-k2.5), but you can force triggering subagents by telling the model to “use/spawn/create subagents” Example prompts: spawn subagents to explore the auth flow, payment integration, and notification system create subagents to map the database queries, trace the API routes, and catalog error handling patterns Web search - when a model needs current information, Ollama handles the search and returns results directly without any additional configuration. Subagents can leverage web search to research topics in parallel and come back with actionable results. Example prompts: research the postgres 18 release notes, audit our queries for deprecated patterns, and create migration tasks create 3 research agents to research how our top 3 competitors price their API tiers, compare against our current pricing, and draft recommendations Recommended models: minimax-m2.5:cloud, glm-5:cloud, kimi-k2.5:cloud

slides.title: AI Updates Mac mini AI agent automates accounting
slides.text: AI Updates Mac mini AI agent automates accounting tasks Using only browser-based control, without direct APIs After reviewing existing skills in their cloud code setup, they focus on two: an accounting skill for Accounting.com and a Gmail skill for navigating email First, they show the agent creating a draft invoice from structured instructions, filling in customer, amount, and line items, fixing duplicates, saving the draft, then downloading the PDF and composing an email in Gmail with subject, body text, and the invoice attached. They then update the accounting skill with this workflow. Next, they combine the Gmail and accounting skills so the agent scans Gmail for PDF invoices, extracts details, and logs them as bills in the accounting software, correctly setting vendor, dates, amounts, and status. The video concludes with the creator impressed but still preferring to review drafts manually. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S0GquerAcRU https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7lyU_CKp3WA Matthew Berman explains how he uses OpenClaw OpenClaw has become a central, always-on personal AI assistant that runs locally on his MacBook and touches nearly every part of his work and life OpenClaw is an open-source framework that connects top language models to chat apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, and Slack, with a configurable personality defined in identity.md and soul.md and a powerful memory system that stores notes and preferences in local Markdown and SQLite databases He walks through many automations he has built: a no-code personal CRM, a Fathom-driven meeting-to-action-items pipeline, a knowledge base that ingests links and X posts, nightly “business” and “security” councils, social and video-idea tracking, daily briefings, cron-based schedules, backups to Git/GDrive, and even a food journal that helped identify dietary triggers He stresses security hardening, prompt-injection defenses, encryption, and versioned backups, and promises to share all prompts so viewers can replicate his setup. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8kNv3rjQaVA

slides.text: AI Updates Beginner vs Expert Prompting https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l-4XPvZmijo 1. Beginner - ask the AI to write about your topic as a beginner who only understands surface-level principles and keep it realistic 2. Expert - ask the AI to rewrite that exact same content as someone who deeply understands core mechanisms, focusing on leverage points and trade-offs 3. The Difference (Evolution) - ask the AI to list the conceptual shifts between the two versions. Specifically, ask what changed in terms of assumptions, priorities, and decision-making For even deeper structural clarity, you can use a single advanced prompt to map the evolution of thinking: What does the novice overestimate? What does the expert deliberately ignore? What assumptions disappear over time? What becomes simpler once mechanics are understood? Brian Casel running 4 OpenClaw Agents on Mac Mini He manages his "team" through Slack, using separate bots for each agent (coding, content scheduling,  "glue work") He uses Claude via Open Router to avoid account bans https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bzWI3Dil9Ig

slides.title: AI Updates Agent Era - ByteDance’s Doubao 2.0
slides.text: AI Updates Agent Era - ByteDance’s Doubao 2.0 - China’s most widely used AI app, with over 155 million weekly users, launched to compete with OpenAI’s GPT‑5.2 and Google’s Gemini 3 Pro. It emphasizes extreme cost efficiency for long‑running AI agents. - Alibaba’s Qwen 3.5 - Backed by a $400 million user‑incentive campaign, Qwen’s daily active users jumped from 7 million to 58 million. The model features native multimodality and 397 billion parameters. - Google DeepMind’s Alletheia - A specialized agent for mathematical research that autonomously authored a peer‑reviewed paper and solved four open conjectures. AI - human crisis of literacy and accountability Dr. McCoy’s reframes the “AI crisis” as a human crisis of literacy and accountability, not a battle against sentient machines She outlines three forms of misuse—the Oracle Effect (treating AI as infallible), Expertise Illusion (using it without understanding), and Responsibility Gap (blaming the tool for human errors). McCoy argues that fear of an AI-driven jobs apocalypse ignores history: like the printing press or ATMs, new tech disrupts before it expands opportunity. Citing the World Economic Forum, she notes AI could replace 92 million jobs but create 170 million more. The real divide, she says, will be AI users vs. AI avoiders. The true threat is letting “agreeable” models reinforce ignorance, while the opportunity lies with those who use AI thoughtfully—as leverage, not as a crutch for missing expertise. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zVj4b_uImZE Aletheia comes from Ancient Greek and literally means “truth,” in the sense of “unconcealed” or “unhidden” reality

slides.title: Claude Code 1 hour Tutorial https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fYX6hHC9FhQ Install Visual
slides.text: Claude Code 1 hour Tutorial https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fYX6hHC9FhQ Install Visual Studio Code, add Claude Code extension Login, use max subscription Create a folder for your project " AI Marketing Officer " Give permissions for most non-destructive actions Build a first “post” skill that takes either a topic or a YouTube/TikTok link, uses an external research agent (like Perplexity) to gather information, then drafts and publishes a social post plus an optional visual via tools like Blot or existing local images - for example, posting to Twitter/X and LinkedIn (using API), logging what was published, and letting you choose between multiple draft options before posting Define a brand-voice layer by adding platform-specific writing samples into a `skill.md` file (or by scraping influencers like Alex Hormozi for Twitter and Justin Welsh for LinkedIn as initial style references). Claude uses these samples to rewrite and upgrade generic drafts into content that better matches your desired tone for each platform You then add “quality gates” using Claude Code hooks: small scripts that automatically run before publishing to enforce rules such as banning certain punctuation (like em dashes), blocking disallowed keywords, or constraining color schemes in visuals. Every post must pass these checks before it can be published, so the system can enforce consistent quality and brand safety without manual review each time After that, the tutorial introduces sub-agents, where each sub-agent is responsible for one platform and runs in parallel to handle its own formatting, scheduling, and publishing. This multi-agent setup lets the same core content be adapted and pushed to multiple platforms asynchronously, improving speed and reliability for multi-platform campaigns Finally, you create a second planning skill that, from a single sentence brief, proposes a full weekly content calendar, lets you review and edit the plan and drafts, then schedules posts on your calendar once approved Keep a personal `claude.md` memory file with prompts, patterns, and lessons learned so Claude can steadily improve at working with your specific workflows over time

slides.title: AI Updates Use Claude Code to implement OpenClaw
slides.text: AI Updates Use Claude Code to implement OpenClaw functions https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BYEaLMnfIjg Tutorial - build AI agent  using Claude Code and Telegram. tech stack: Bun (JavaScript runtime), Claude Code (subscription-based), creating a Telegram bot through BotFather, and configuring a Supabase database for memory storage Google's open-source Python library Lang Extract https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l2BGg4ZwsH8 https://github.com/google/langextract - 33K stars Lang Extract provides precise source grounding, allowing every extracted piece of information to be traced back to its exact origin in the source text Learn 90% Of Claude Code Agent Teams in 22 Minutes (Opus 4.6) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cSkoaCCmq0w Tutorial - use Claude Code's new agent teams feature in Opus 4.6 Three modes: default (single session) sub-agent (one main session with delegated tasks) agent teams (multiple independent sessions) Use T-Max for split terminal windows Session management, token conservation strategies, using different models for cost efficiency, and proper team shutdown procedures

slides.title: AI Updates Automate daily tasks with Claude Code
slides.text: AI Updates Automate daily tasks with Claude Code https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2bsfQThGXxc Create folders (skills, context, outputs, scripts) Common mistakes: using Claude like a chatbot, not providing proper context, failing to use planning loops, and not utilizing scripts for external data Create reusable command prompts Start fresh sessions with priming commands to avoid context bloat How to create custom Claude Code workflows - SKILL.md https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XtjZsFtUQqw Find relevant YouTube channels, copy their transcripts, use Claude to create a skill file from those transcripts Use Gina.ai for web scraping and Gemini API for image generation VisionClaw = Meta Ray-Ban glasses + AI Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t9Ps1cUIYCc Users to interact with an assistant through voice commands while the AI sees through the glasses' camera Created by student founder Shawn Example: adding products to Amazon cart just by looking at them The tool is free and uses Gemini AI with OpenClaw integration Use cases: real estate agents taking notes during property tours, mechanics getting instant diagnostic help, teachers answering student questions on-demand, and personal shopping assistants

slides.title: AI Updates Voxtral Realtime speech recognition Natively streaming
slides.text: AI Updates Voxtral Realtime speech recognition Natively streaming automatic speech recognition model that matches offline transcription quality at sub-second latency Unlike approaches that adapt offline models through chunking or sliding windows, Voxtral Realtime is trained end-to-end for streaming, with explicit alignment between audio and text streams Open weights - Apache 2.0 license. https://huggingface.co/papers/2602.11298
